title: NouSR scenario
description: One scenario = one set of battle conditions and one or more teams that are each simulated under exactly those conditions, so their results are on one scale. Keys are snake_case to match the HSR-Scanner v4 build format this file sits beside.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, for editor completion.

format.description: Identifies the file type, the way HSR-Scanner files carry "source".

version.description: Version of this schema. Goes up only on a breaking change.

game_version.description: Game version the scenario was written for, e.g. "4.7". The simulator refuses a scenario whose game version it does not model.

account.description: Where builds come from. Either a path to an HSR-Scanner v4 JSON file, relative to this scenario file, or that JSON inline (which makes the scenario self-contained and shareable). Leave out to run every member on standard relics.

teams.description: Each team is simulated separately under the same battle and enemies. Team ids must be unique.

notes.description: Free text for people. The simulator ignores it.

slug.description: A short name chosen by the author: lower-case letters, digits and underscores.

scan_v4.description: An HSR-Scanner v4 export (https://github.com/kel-z/HSR-Scanner). Reliquary Archiver writes the same shape. Only the parts NouSR reads are checked here.

relic_v4.description: One relic exactly as HSR-Scanner v4 writes it.

mode.description: Game mode. Sets the cycle lengths: Memory of Chaos is 150 AV for the first cycle, then 100. Other modes are on the roadmap.

period.description: Id of the period module (Memory Turbulence) to apply, e.g. "moc-2026-11-survival-of-the-fittest". null or absent = none.

start.description: Starting state. Defaults are the Memory of Chaos defaults from DESIGN.md decision 6.

energy.description: Starting energy as a share of each character's maximum.

techniques.description: Whether every member's technique is used before the battle.

profile.description: Id of an enemy profile. v1 ships one: "generic-moc".

counts.description: Number of enemies on the field. Each value is its own run with its own results, e.g. [1, 3, 5].

weaknesses.description: Which elements the enemies are weak to. "all" makes every team hit a weakness, which keeps teams of different elements comparable; a list models a specific stage.

members.description: In party order, left to right. Member keys must be unique within the team.

policy.description: The team's priority script. Whenever someone can act, the list is read top to bottom and the first rule that applies is taken. A rule applies when its unit can use that action right now and every entry in "when" holds. Ultimate rules are checked between any two actions; basic and skill rules only on that unit's own turn. A turn on which no rule applies is an error, so every unit needs an unconditional fallback.

key.description: How policy rules refer to this member, e.g. "acheron".

character.description: Game character id as a string, as in HSR-Scanner, e.g. "1308" for Acheron.

ability_version.description: Same field as HSR-Scanner v4. 0 = the original kit, 1 = the buffed (Nova Flare) kit. If absent: taken from the account scan, else the newest version.

eidolon.description: Overrides the account scan. Required when there is no account.

affinitive_eidolon.description: The scan format has no field for this, so it is always set here.

light_cone.description: Overrides the account scan. Required when there is no account.

id.description: Game light cone id as a string, e.g. "23024".

relics.description: "equipped": the relics the account scan shows on this character. "standard": Fribbels' benchmark build for this character. A list: exactly these relics, each given either as the "_uid" of a relic in the account scan or as a full HSR-Scanner v4 relic object. Default: "equipped" when there is an account, otherwise "standard".

unit.description: Key of the member this rule is for.

use.description: The action. "basic", "skill" and "ultimate" exist for everyone; a kit may add its own (for example an enhanced basic). The simulator rejects a name the unit's kit does not have.

target.description: Who the action is aimed at, where the kit needs one: a member key for an ally-targeted action. Enemy-targeted actions always aim at the primary target.

when.description: All must hold. Absent or empty = always.

what.description: A quantity in the live state, as a dotted path. "team.skill_points", "battle.cycle", or "<member key>.<quantity>" such as "acheron.slashed_dream". Each kit publishes the quantities it has; the simulator rejects a path it does not know.

min.description: Holds when the quantity is at least this.

max.description: Holds when the quantity is at most this.
